title: Paul McCartney signs new deal with EMI and Capitol Records | 1975
content:
A new four-year record deal between Paul McCartney and EMI/Capitol Records was announced on 15 May 1975.

McCartney’s previous deal was renegotiated following the settlement of The Beatles’ business issues. He was in a strong position, following the success of Band On The Run, and with its follow-up, Venus And Mars, due out at the end of the month.

His father-in-law Lee Eastman secured a reported artist royalty rate of 24%, or 54 pence for every album sold in the UK, and 7p per single. This was significantly higher than the 17.5% that The Beatles had had since 1969. Eastman also arranged for McCartney to own all his solo album masters.

He also received an advance of around $3,300,000 upon renewing with EMI/Capitol, and was given ownership of Capitol’s share in Morley Music. The latter included the publishing rights to a number of standards, plus – crucially – The Beatles’ ‘Love Me Do’ and ‘PS I Love You’.

Capitol Records and Paul McCartney are delighted to announce that they have concluded an exclusive recording agreement for the USA, Canada and Japan. A separate agreement covering all other territories of the world has been concluded between Mr. McCartney and EMI Records. The first recording under the new agreement, the album Venus And Mars, will be released worldwide in May on the Capitol label.
Capitol Records press release
